- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:307-323, 349-354 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Records are read in session-filename order, but `group_patterns` treats that order as chronological when setting `last_ts`, `example`, and `allow_rule`.
  WHY: Session filenames are not timestamps, so a pattern occurring in multiple session files can display an older occurrence as the latest example and allowlist diagnosis.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:275-282, 352-354 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The production copy checks every Bash record against this checkout’s settings without verifying that the record’s cwd belongs to this checkout.
  WHY: Logs span sessions, so a command from another checkout can be reported as already allowlisted even though this checkout’s rule did not apply where the command ran.
- tests/test_permission_prompts.py:567 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The alleged literal newline escapes in the `"origin/newer"` test data are not present; the source describes valid branch-path strings and reports no runtime defect.
  WHY: The reviewer states that the strings use a forward slash and that the assertions match the intended branch-path semantics, so no fix is needed.

  WHY: The `:*` rewrite and only-wildcard bare-command check are reported as correct, so no runtime defect exists.

  PROBLEM: The function rewrites `:*` suffix rules to ` *` suffix rules at line 286-287, equating the two forms. This is documented in the Claude Code permissions docs as correct: "The `:*` suffix is an equivalent way to write a trailing wildcard." The only-wildcard bare-command check at line 288 then correctly restricts `Bash(git merge *)` matching bare `git merge` to rules whose sole wildcard is the trailing `*`. No runtime defect exists.
  WHY IT FAILS AT RUNTIME: Does not fail. The matcher semantics match the documented Claude Code permissions rules. The round-1 verdict comment at entry[13] in the PR discussion confirms this was reviewed and accepted.
